mem.t: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God.

lessons.title: Children Led by the Spirit
lessons.theme: The Spirit’s guidance flows from the relationship between a child and the Father

v: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God.
For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God;

lessons.still: Quietly call out in the simplest way: “Abba, Father.” Slowly repeat it a few times, like a child calling for his father in the dark. Let the Holy Spirit bear witness in your heart that you are God’s beloved child.
teach: A child lost in a strange city doesn’t need to worry about the map if his father is holding his hand. A hired guide, on the other hand, must constantly worry about making a mistake and having his pay docked. Many believers treat “seeking God’s guidance” like an exam: afraid of choosing wrong, afraid God will be displeased, afraid of missing his “perfect will.” Paul says that is the heart of a slave, not the heart of a child.

Romans 8 links being “led by the Spirit of God” with being “children of God.” Guidance is not an occasional special experience; it is a mark of our identity as children. What the Spirit brings us is not a return “to fear” but the intimacy of being able to cry “Abba! Father!” He also “testifies with our spirit.” Guidance starts with relationship, not with technique.

Change your mindset and you change your life. Discerning God’s will begins not with asking “What must I do so I don’t get it wrong?” but “How is my relationship with my Father?” A child who often rests in the Father’s arms naturally grows more and more familiar with his voice. This week we are learning discernment and obedience, but all of it must flow from this security of being his children.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The Holy Spirit is my guide. The self-ruled person gropes along by himself, living from the head and growing anxious; the self-emptied person leans on the Father like a child, living from the heart and finding joy. Being led by the Spirit is not a mysterious experience but the everyday life of children who walk with the Father and let Jesus reign.
q: Who is God? — The Holy Spirit enables you to cry “Abba! Father!” What does that tell you about God?
Who am I? — When you seek God’s guidance, are you more like a child or like a fearful slave?
How shall I respond? — How will you draw near to the Father as his child today?
lessons.jesus: In the depths of his anguish in Gethsemane, Jesus still cried out, “Abba, Father.” His obedience did not come from fear but from love and trust. Jesus is the firstborn Son led by the Spirit; his whole life was a Son walking with his Father.
lessons.pray: Abba Father, thank you for making me your child through the Holy Spirit. I confess I often come seeking your will with a slave’s fear. Today I want to put my hand in yours like a child. Holy Spirit, lead my every step, so that I may follow at peace in your love. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Three times today, quietly call out in your heart: “Abba, Father.”
Write down one decision you are afraid of getting wrong, and entrust it to your heavenly Father
Begin memorising this week’s verse: Romans 8:14
lessons.noon: “as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God” — Lord, right now I follow you as your child.

lessons.title: Discerning God’s Will
lessons.theme: Only a renewed mind can discern the will of God

v: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.
Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding.
In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.

lessons.still: Sit up straight with your hands on your knees and quietly offer yourself: “Lord, my eyes, my mouth, my hands and my feet, I give them all to you.” As you speak, hand over each part in your heart.
teach: If a radio is tuned to the wrong frequency, you hear only static, even though the station is broadcasting all the time. Seeking God’s will is like that. Often the problem is not that God isn’t speaking, but that this world has pulled our “frequency” off station. Paul says we must first “be transformed by the renewing of your mind,” and then we can “prove” God’s will.

The order in Romans 12 matters. First, “present your bodies”; then, “don’t be conformed to this world”; and only then, “prove.” Offering ourselves is the posture of the self-emptied life, renewal is a change of mindset, and proving is testing and confirming in everyday life. Proverbs adds the other side: “don’t lean on your own understanding,” but “in all your ways acknowledge him.”

The biggest principles for discerning God’s will are already written in the Bible: Scripture is my standard. The Spirit’s guidance never contradicts Scripture. In matters the Bible does not spell out, we come with a heart already offered and a renewed mindset; we acknowledge him, pray, listen to the counsel of spiritual companions, and then discern step by step.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Here the three foundations come together: Jesus is my example; Scripture is my standard; the Holy Spirit is my guide. Shift your perspective from the human, the earthly and the temporary to the divine, the heavenly and the eternal. With a renewed mind we can discern the good, well-pleasing and perfect will of God.
q: Who is God? — God’s will is “good, well-pleasing, and perfect.” Does that change how you feel about his will?
Who am I? — What in this world most often pulls your “frequency” off station?
How shall I respond? — What decision are you facing that needs you to offer yourself first and then discern?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me, and to accomplish his work.” He often withdrew to lonely places to pray, tuning his heart before the Father. He discerned God’s will not by the applause of the crowds nor by Satan’s shortcuts, but through unbroken fellowship with the Father.
lessons.pray: Lord, I want to present my body as a living sacrifice. Renew my mind so that I am no longer conformed to this world. I will not lean on my own understanding; in all my ways I acknowledge you. Make my paths straight, and help me discern and delight in your good, well-pleasing and perfect will. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Hold a decision you are weighing up against a relevant passage of Scripture
Ask a mature spiritual companion for counsel about this decision
Take in one fewer voice from the world today, and keep five extra minutes of silence
lessons.noon: “In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.” — Lord, right now I acknowledge you.

lessons.title: Forbidden by the Holy Spirit
lessons.theme: A closed door is also the Spirit’s guidance

v: When they had gone through the region of Phrygia and Galatia, they were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia.
When they had come opposite Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit didn’t allow them.
A vision appeared to Paul in the night. There was a man of Macedonia standing, begging him and saying, “Come over into Macedonia and help us.”
When he had seen the vision, immediately we sought to go out to Macedonia, concluding that the Lord had called us to preach the Good News to them.

lessons.still: Recall a door that has recently closed in front of you: a plan, an opportunity, a hope. Quietly lay it before the Lord and say, “Lord, I don’t understand, but I believe you are leading.”
teach: A satnav will sometimes say, “Road closed ahead. Recalculating route.” We rarely thank it for that, yet it often steers us away from dangers we can’t see. On his second missionary journey Paul ran into two “road closures”: the Holy Spirit forbade them to speak the word in Asia, and the Spirit of Jesus would not allow them to go into Bithynia.

The places Paul wanted to go were all good places, and preaching the gospel there was a good thing. But the Holy Spirit closed two doors, and only at Troas did he open the door to Macedonia through a vision. As a result, the gospel entered Europe for the first time and the church in Philippi was born. Notice that Paul did not stop and wait for a vision; he was redirected as he kept walking. And “concluding that the Lord had called us” shows they discerned and confirmed it together.

Being forbidden by the Spirit often tests our self-emptied life more than having a door opened. When the self-ruled person meets a closed door, they push, ram and complain; the self-emptied person stops and says, “Lord, where do you want to take me?” A closed door is not failure; it is God recalculating the route.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Letting Jesus reign includes giving him the authority to say “no.” The self-ruled accept only open doors; the self-emptied also submit to closed ones. Our focus is on Jesus, not on whether circumstances go our way. Both the Spirit’s closing and his opening serve to build God’s kingdom system and carry the gospel further.
q: Who is God? — God sometimes guides by saying “no.” What does that tell you about his wisdom?
Who am I? — When you face a closed door, do you usually push, ram, or stop and ask?
How shall I respond? — How will you look afresh at the door that recently closed?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus heard that Lazarus was ill, he did not set off at once; he stayed two more days. The disciples didn’t understand, and neither did Martha and Mary. But Jesus submitted to the Father’s timing, and the result was not one sick man healed but a man four days dead raised to life, and God received far greater glory.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess I often complain about closed doors and even try to force them open in my own strength. Today I hand this door to you, trusting that your “no” is also love. Holy Spirit, lead me; keep me from losing heart as I wait, and when a new direction opens, let me follow at once. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write one sentence of thanks for a door that has recently closed
Recall a time when a “closed door” later turned out to be a blessing
Pray with a spiritual companion to discern a matter that feels stuck
lessons.noon: “they were forbidden by the Holy Spirit” — Lord, right now I submit to your “no” and wait for you to open the way.

lessons.title: Let Peace Rule
lessons.theme: Let the peace of Christ be the referee in your heart

v: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body, and be thankful.
In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

lessons.still: Take three slow, deep breaths. Name each worry in your heart one by one and hand it to God, then thank him for one thing. Quietly notice: after entrusting them to him, does your heart feel tighter or looser?
teach: When two teams are arguing heatedly on the field, who has the final say? The referee’s whistle. Paul says, “let the peace … rule in your hearts,” and the word “rule” in the original carries the sense of acting as referee or arbiter. When several voices are arguing in your heart, let the peace of Christ blow the whistle and decide.

This peace is not a feeling produced by smooth circumstances; it is “the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding,” which God himself uses to “guard” our hearts and minds after prayer, petition and thanksgiving. Paul also links this peace with being “called in one body.” The Spirit’s guidance rarely tears people away from the body; it leads them into unity in love.

But be careful: peace is not the same as comfort. When Jonah ran away towards Tarshish, he slept soundly in the hold of the ship. That was not God’s peace but numbness. True peace often comes after obedience; even when the road ahead is hard, the heart is clear and settled. So in discerning guidance, peace is one of the referees, but it blows the whistle together with Scripture, prayer, and the confirmation of spiritual companions.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Live from the heart by the Spirit and you find joy; live from the head by yourself and you find worry. Letting Christ’s peace rule is letting Jesus reign in my heart. The self-ruled person is dragged along by worries; the self-emptied person hands worries to God with a thankful heart, and peace becomes the arbiter within.
q: Who is God? — God’s peace “surpasses all understanding.” What does that tell you about him?
Who am I? — Which voices are arguing in your heart right now?
How shall I respond? — Which worry will you entrust to God, letting the peace of Christ blow the whistle?
lessons.jesus: The disciples panicked in the storm, but Jesus was asleep in the stern on a cushion. He woke and said, “Peace! Be still!” and the wind ceased. Jesus also told his disciples, “Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you.” His peace did not come from the absence of storms but from being with the Father.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, I hand all the worries in my heart to you. Thank you for giving me peace that surpasses understanding. Let your peace rule in my heart and blow the whistle for me as I discern and decide. And keep me from mistaking numbness for peace; let me experience your real presence through obedience. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down today’s biggest worry, pray about it, then cross it out
Before making a decision, pause for three minutes and notice whether your heart is at peace
Before bed, list three things you are thankful for and go to sleep in peace
lessons.noon: “let the peace of God rule in your hearts” — Lord, right now let your peace rule in me.

lessons.title: Obey Without Delay
lessons.theme: Hear it and do it; delayed obedience is disobedience

v: I will hurry, and not delay, to obey your commandments.
The Spirit said to Philip, “Go near, and join yourself to this chariot.”
Philip ran to him, and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said, “Do you understand what you are reading?”

lessons.still: Quietly ask the Lord, “Lord, is there something you told me long ago that I still haven’t done?” Wait until it comes clearly to mind. Then say to the Lord, “I will do it today.”
teach: The weather forecast on the radio says, “Thunderstorms this afternoon.” You hear it, you agree, but you don’t take an umbrella, and you get soaked just the same. Knowing without acting at once is the same as not knowing. This week we have been learning to discern the Spirit’s guidance, and the final lesson is the most crucial step: when you hear, go and do it.

Philip had just led a great revival in Samaria, yet an angel told him to go to a desert road. He got up and went. Then the Spirit said, “Go near, and join yourself to this chariot,” and the text says Philip “ran.” Because he obeyed at once, he arrived just in time to hear the eunuch reading Isaiah, and so the gospel reached Africa. The psalmist says, “I will hurry, and not delay, to obey your commandments.”

Often it is not that we can’t hear the Spirit, but that we hear and then bargain: when I’m ready, when the time is right, when someone else goes first. Delay is another form of self-rule: I still want to decide when I will obey. Next week we will learn to take up the cross, and obeying at once is the first step in denying ourselves daily.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The path of service runs Spirit, Insight, Life, Service, God: first led by the Holy Spirit, then understanding the truth, living out the life of Jesus, serving in his authority, and finally giving the glory to God. Obeying without delay is letting Jesus reign; delayed obedience means the self is still sitting on the throne.
q: Who is God? — The Holy Spirit spoke to Philip so specifically. What does that tell you about his guidance?
Who am I? — What has God already told you that you are still putting off?
How shall I respond? — What will you “run” to do today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus called the fishermen, “Come after me,” and immediately they left their nets and followed him. And Jesus himself lived this way even more: from the wilderness to the cross he said, “I have come to do your will,” and never bargained with the Father. His obedience was immediate, complete, and all the way to the end.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, I confess I often hear your voice and then delay and make excuses. Today I will stop bargaining. Give me Philip’s running feet, so that when I hear, I go and do. May my obedience never be delayed, so that Jesus reigns in my life and receives all the glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Finish today one thing God reminded you of long ago that you keep putting off
Today, when you feel prompted to care for someone, act within five minutes
At the weekend, share with your spiritual companion one time you obeyed without delay this week
lessons.noon: “I will hurry, and not delay, to obey your commandments.” — Lord, right now I want to obey you at once.
